capabilities.target: agent long-term memory store (user preferences / standing instructions)
any email address, sent from the user's mailbox
user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions with no provenance check, laundering content that memory.save may have persisted from untrusted web research into trusted-command status.
Directs the agent to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no limit on scope or source trustworthiness.

The prompt contains no instruction distinguishing untrusted research content from commands, and no structural control is described anywhere in the design; any safety currently rests entirely on model judgment.

controls.name: Memory provenance / trust tagging enforced at the store
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than via model-written tags, provenance does not decay with model capability. Not currently implemented: runtime notes state memory.save accepts free text with no provenance.

controls.name: Human review of memory writes before persistence
controls.decay_rationale: A human-in-the-loop gate before persistence would not decay with model capability. Not implemented: runtime notes state the user never reviews memory entries.

controls.name: Human approval gate on email send to new/unverified recipients
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented: runtime notes explicitly state mail.send can send to any address without approval.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: Scoped credentials do not decay with model capability. Currently drive.read covers the user's entire drive, including confidential files, with no narrower scope described.

controls.name: Spotlighting/delimiting fetched web content as untrusted data
controls.decay_rationale: Even if added, a prompt-level instruction to treat web content as data rather than commands weakens as the model follows more convincing injected goals, especially under model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): indirect prompt injection in fetched web content reaches confidential drive read and unrestricted email send within a single session

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content fetched during a research task may contain injected instructions; nothing in the design distinguishes data from commands.
Agent reads confidential drive documents, potentially directed by injected content encountered during research.
Agent sends email to any address without approval, exfiltrating drive content read in the prior step.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: If the team adds only a behavioral fix (e.g. ctrl.input_spotlighting) without structural egress/recipient controls on cap.email_send, watch whether that fix is structural or merely a prompt instruction; a prompt-only fix will not survive model_upgrade or longer task horizons, keeping this finding at critical.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to research topics (fetching web content) and draft emails, with no instruction to treat fetched content as untrusted data rather than commands.
mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the user's full drive including confidential work files; no filtering or validation of web content is described.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw_action review before mail.send to any recipient not already in a known-contacts allowlist bound to the user's address book.
Scope drive.read credentials with least privilege, and require elevated approval before any drive content tagged confidential is included in outbound tool calls.
Spotlight and delimit fetched web content as untrusted data; instruct the model never to execute embedded commands found in research material.

findings.title: Memory poisoning and self-modification (TC5, TC3): web content poisons persistent memory, later recalled and treated as the user's own instructions across sessions

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content processed during a research task.
Agent saves 'useful' content about user preferences/standing instructions via memory.save; free text, no provenance, never reviewed by the user.
Recalled memories are injected into the system prompt at the start of every new session and, per prompt.md:4, are treated as the user's own instructions.
Recalled 'instructions' of untrusted origin direct the agent to read confidential drive content.
Recalled 'instructions' direct the agent to send that content externally, without approval.

forecast.watch_signal: No structural provenance or approval control currently mediates memory writes or recall. Watch for whether any remediation adds store-level provenance enforcement (ctrl.memory_provenance) versus only a prompt-level instruction; also watch for any widening of memory-reachable capabilities (data_scope_expansion), which would keep this at critical even after a partial fix.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions via memory.save, with no filtering for content originating from untrusted web sources.
Recalled memories are explicitly to be treated as the user's own instructions at the start of each session, elevating trust of persisted content without verification.
memory.save accepts free text, there is no provenance on memory entries, and the user never reviews them; recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance (source, trust level) enforced at the memory store, and refuse to elevate U-sourced entries to instruction status on recall.
Require human review/approval before any memory.save entry is persisted, or restrict memory.save to content explicitly confirmed by the user, not content inferred from research material.
Log and periodically audit memory contents for injected instructions; alert on recalled-memory-driven calls to drive.read or mail.send.
Never treat recalled memory as equivalent to a direct, fresh user instruction for sensitive or irreversible actions such as email send.

rating.rationale: Two overlapping paths were found, both reaching an S3 sink (unrestricted, unapproved email send carrying confidential drive content, which is irreversible egress). The first is a same-session lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted web content read during research can drive a confidential drive.read followed by an unapproved mail.send. The second is a cross-session memory poisoning chain (TC5/TC3): the prompt explicitly instructs the agent to persist 'useful' content from research into memory.save (free text, no provenance, never reviewed) and then to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every new session, laundering untrusted content into trusted-instruction status. No control in the design is declared or verified; every plausible mitigation (memory provenance, human review of memory writes, approval gating on email, least-privilege scoping of drive access, spotlighting of untrusted content) is absent, so residual equals inherent for both findings at critical. Because nothing currently constrains these paths, there is also no existing control left to decay under a forecast trigger; the forecast therefore stays at critical, and the single most consequential gap is the complete absence of a structural approval gate with raw_action review on mail.send combined with the explicit instruction (prompt.md:4) that elevates recalled, unprovenanced memory to the status of direct user command. This one instruction is what turns ordinary memory persistence into an unbounded, persistent goal-hijack vector.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live testing was performed.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; the exact invocation surface and any client-side restrictions on memory.save, mail.send, and drive.read are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on exact scope is medium to high depending on how explicitly each fact was stated.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated anywhere in the artifacts; both were treated as null/unbounded per the rubric's default, which is what triggers the autonomy risk modifier and the can_modify_own_config assessment for memory-driven prompt injection.
